root_cause_conclusion: SUPPORTED method-external PX4-to-MicroXRCE entity-creation startup backlog; simultaneous controller discovery/activation is a possible amplifier

N24.tail_pattern: UAV20-24 never produced PX4 odometry/status writers; UAV19 produced them only at the 300 s timeout boundary; UAV17 had finite fresh state but never armed/offboard

H1.evidence: All simulator TCP connections formed, but timesync RTT rose from <=220 ms at N20 to 568/832/2420 ms at N24/N28/N32; PX4 height-estimate instability, transient failsafe logs, and strongly displaced final states appeared only in failed larger-N runs.

H2.evidence: N24 client keys 21-25 created a participant and 29 readers each but zero output writers; client 20 completed writers only at timeout. The same startup-order tail truncation occurred at N28/N32.

H3.evidence: v1 created all controllers together (552 neighbor subscriptions at N24) and initiated arm/offboard concurrently. Writer backlog was already present before controller launch, so this cannot be the sole cause, but it can amplify discovery and activation contention.

H4.evidence: The same audited deterministic grid and matching ENU offsets passed at N20; failures form a startup-order tail, not a spatial row/coordinate pattern; every simulator TCP port matched its UAV ID.

H5.evidence: Load increased with N and timing degradation was visible, but N24 one-minute load 12.3 remained below 24 logical CPUs and >17 GiB memory remained available. No direct CPU exhaustion or OOM evidence exists; reliable RTF was unavailable.

H6.evidence: PX4 instances were launched roughly one model-spawn apart without waiting for the preceding XRCE output entities. Entity completion lag accumulated by launch order: N24 UAV19 completed only at timeout while later clients never completed.
